inspiration.observed_pattern: A window query uses NTH_VALUE to project the second-longest value within each partition, with an explicit full-partition frame for rows beyond the first one.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored album-track report. Fixed tracks are partitioned by album and ordered by descending duration with a track-ID tie-breaker; one full-frame NTH_VALUE projection repeats the second-longest title on every row, while a default-frame projection exposes the current-row boundary. SQLite table names, track data, and example labels are not copied.

fixture_notes: Album 501 has three tracks ordered by 420, 360, and 300 seconds; album 502 has two tracks ordered by 515 and 250 seconds. The explicit track ID tie-breaker makes every window order unique, and the full-frame projection must expose each album's second-longest title on all rows.
determinism_notes: Album IDs, track IDs, titles, durations, frame clauses, and final ordering are fixed; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE album_tracks (track_id INT PRIMARY KEY, album_id INT NOT NULL, track_title VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, duration_seconds INT NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO album_tracks VALUES (4101, 501, 'Dawn Signal', 420), (4102, 501, 'Harbor Lights', 360), (4103, 501, 'Night Relay', 300), (4201, 502, 'Copper Road', 515), (4202, 502, 'Glass Station', 250)

steps.sql: SELECT album_id, track_id, track_title, duration_seconds, NTH_VALUE(track_title, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY album_id ORDER BY duration_seconds DESC, track_id ASC ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS second_longest_title FROM album_tracks ORDER BY album_id, duration_seconds DESC, track_id

SELECT album_id, track_id, NTH_VALUE(track_title, 2) OVER (PARTITION BY album_id ORDER BY duration_seconds DESC, track_id ASC) AS default_frame_second_title FROM album_tracks ORDER BY album_id, duration_seconds DESC, track_id
